findings.title: A weapon-enchant (WPN_ENCH) macro deferred in combat is flushed as a single-item macro, losing /use 16 and /use 17 and the off-hand line
findings.evidence: A per-hand write queued in combat stores only itemID = mhPick or ohPick, and entry.cat is nil. FlushPending then rebuilds it through M.SetMacro, which only knows the single-item shape. A scratch probe gave '#showtooltip / /use item:944001 / /use 16 / /use item:944002 / /use 17' out of combat, but '#showtooltip / /use item:944003' after a deferral and flush. The fingerprint stores the wrong body, so nothing corrects it until some later recompute. Reachable through /cm rewritemacros in combat (documented as allowed), a weapon swap mid-fight, or an oil looted or used up mid-fight. The FlushPending test covers KCM_FOOD only.
findings.remediation: C-01: FlushPending replays the queued body. Composites keep pcall(M.SetCompositeMacro, entry.cat, nil). Every other entry calls pcall(commitMacro, name, entry.body, entry.itemID, entry.catKey) through the one write tail, with no second write path (events-frames-taint-§4). Characterization first (the FOOD case at :330), then two red-first cases: a per-hand flush keeps /use 16 and /use 17, and /cm rewritemacros in combat keeps the WPN_ENCH body. About +2 cases; regenerate test-cases.md and the badge.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. modules/MacroManager.lua:411-420 queueForCombat stores body, itemID and catKey, and leaves cat nil for non-composites. SetWeaponEnchantMacro (:525-532) passes iconItemID = mhPick or ohPick. FlushPending (:598-602) sends every non-composite through M.SetMacro(name, entry.itemID, entry.catKey), and that rebuilds the body with BuildBody as a single-item body (:505-519). commitMacro then fingerprints that wrong body (:486-491). The only flush test (tests/test_macromanager.lua:330) covers KCM_FOOD. I lowered severity from high to medium. The damage lasts only until the next recompute: RecomputeOne (core/ConsumableMaster.lua:127-134) rebuilds the per-hand body, and alreadyApplied sees that lastBody differs, so any later bag or equipment event rewrites the macro. Nothing runs a recompute on regen itself, so the broken macro can last into the next pull if nothing else fires. It is a real but self-healing breakage, not a persistent one. The remediation (replay entry.body through commitMacro, with composites unchanged) is sound and keeps a single write tail.

findings.title: A settings category parked in combat is never registered while the addon is disabled; the panel and Enable checkbox are gone for the session
findings.locations: settings/Panel.lua:1267-1269; core/ConsumableMaster.lua:623-657 (replay at :654-656, stood-down early return at :631-635); core/LifecycleSetup.lua:98-100; settings/OptionsShim.lua:233; tests/test_settingsui_optionsui.lua:769-799
findings.evidence: registerPanel parks the registration under lockdown (registerPending = true). The only replay is at the end of OnRegenEnabled. The stood-down branch unregisters PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED and returns before the replay. When the stand-down finished out of combat, no PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED is registered at all. A probe showed 'stood down: true / parked: true / replays on regen while disabled: 0'. /cm config, bare /cm and the launcher right-click then print the misleading 'settings panel unavailable on this client'. slash-commands-§7 'What MUST survive' names settings-category registration. Existing tests pin the replay only while the addon is enabled.
findings.remediation: C-03 / B2: extract the replay into a named helper (replayParkedSettings / replayParkedRegistration) and call it on both branches, before the stood-down return. Extract, do not branch: OnRegenEnabled is at CCN 15 and should drop to about 12. Add KCM.EnsureRegenForParkedSettings() in core/LifecycleSetup.lua, called from registerPanel's park branch, which registers PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED when stood down. Add red-first cases for a stand-down out of combat and one in combat, with a falsification comment. Add a row to ARCHITECTURE.md 'What SURVIVES'. After upstream A3 lands, call UI.ReplayPending() instead. Run smoke test §6a with the addon disabled.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (What MUST survive); performance-§11; anti-pattern #52; automated-tests-§3
findings.verify_reason: Verified. settings/Panel.lua:1267-1269 parks the registration with registerPending = true. The only replay is at core/ConsumableMaster.lua:654-656, and the stood-down branch at :631-635 unregisters PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED and returns before reaching it. core/LifecycleSetup.lua:98-100 registers regen only when the stand-down itself happened in combat. slash-commands.md 'What MUST survive' names the settings-category registration and the panel body. The existing tests (tests/test_settingsui_optionsui.lua:769-799) cover only the enabled path. The trigger is narrow (a login or /reload in combat, or Blizzard_Settings force-loaded mid-fight, while disabled), but losing the panel and its Enable checkbox for the session is a direct violation of a MUST-survive item, so medium holds. On the remediation: registering PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED while stood down to replay parked setup goes beyond the single sanctioned stand-down registration in slash-commands.md:192. It is justified because it serves setup that MUST survive, but it must be released the moment it fires. The existing stood-down branch already does that, as long as the replay runs before that return.

findings.title: Macro-bar flyout attribute drivers (kcmCombat) stay registered while the addon is disabled; nothing unregisters them
findings.evidence: RegisterAttributeDriver(flyout, 'kcmCombat', '[combat] 1; 0') runs once per slot, up to 15 slots. There is no UnregisterAttributeDriver anywhere in the tree. The disable path unregisters the bar's visibility state driver and clears OnUpdate, but never reaches the flyouts. The secure state-driver manager keeps evaluating these after the player disables the addon.
findings.remediation: B1 / S2-1: add FO.StandDown and FO.StandUp, plus a module-level FLYOUT_COMBAT_DRIVER constant, to modules/MacroBarFlyout.lua. Call FO.StandDown for every built flyout from MB.Update's disable branch, which is already combat-deferred. Re-arm them on the enable path through ensure() and applyVisibility(). Keep the frames rather than rebuilding them. Re-run smoke test §11e.
findings.verify_reason: Verified. modules/MacroBarFlyout.lua:289-290 calls RegisterAttributeDriver(flyout,'kcmCombat','[combat] 1; 0'), and grep finds no UnregisterAttributeDriver anywhere in modules, core or settings. The disable branch of MB.Update (modules/MacroBar.lua:453-461) unregisters only the bar's visibility state driver and clears OnUpdate. slash-commands.md:192 requires secure state and attribute drivers to be stood down, with completion deferred until combat ends. The runtime cost is small (secure driver evaluation), but this is a plain MUST breach, so medium stands.

findings.title: The color validator returns value without copying, so /cm reset <color> stores the dbDefaults table itself; a later profile switch empties the shipped default
findings.evidence: This is the only table validator that does not copy (order and map do; see :929). A probe showed 'stored IS dbDefaults table = true'. Against the real vendored AceDB, SetProfile's removeDefaults nils every channel, leaving the defaults color with 0 entries. For the rest of the session the swatch reads opaque black and /cm get reports fallbacks. The Macro Bar Defaults button is unaffected because it uses CopyTable.
findings.remediation: C-02: the color validator returns a shallow copy (local out = {}; copy the pairs; return out), with a comment explaining why. Add red-first cases: 'resetting a color row stores a copy', and 'a profile switch after a color reset leaves the shipped default intact' (#defaults == 4). The second depends on the mock fix in F-006.
findings.verify_reason: Verified. The color validator in settings/Panel.lua:920-923 returns value as-is, while the order validator (:925-940) documents that it always returns a fresh table because row.default IS the dbDefaults table. The reset applyDefault (settings/Slash.lua:530-533) sends row.default through SetAndRefresh (Panel.lua:974-992), which stores the coerced value, so the default table gets aliased into the profile. The page reset in settings/MacroBar.lua:636-637 already copies for exactly this reason. On a profile switch, AceDB's removeDefaults nils the channels that match the defaults in place on the shared table, which empties the shipped default. The fix is local and correctly routed. OptionsCompose only assigns row.default and is not at fault.

findings.title: The settings panel opened while disabled cannot hydrate item rows ([Loading]), and the code comment claims it can
findings.evidence: The stand-down unregisters GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED and drops the options target's PANEL_REFRESH subscription, and those are the only hydration triggers. Rows opened in a fresh session sit on [Loading]. The comment documents the opposite and cites a toggle onChange in settings/Panel.lua that no longer exists. slash-commands-§7 records the panel-refresh question as 'Recorded, not ruled', so this is a behavior regression plus a false comment, not a compliance finding.
findings.remediation: C-04: rewrite the comment truthfully and remove the dead pointer. Add a Known Limitations bullet to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Deferred for an owner decision at CP2: panel-owned hydration while disabled through LibKa0s-Item LoadItem (core/ItemSetup.lua:14-16 declines it today). Either open a tracked issue or record the behavior as accepted.
findings.verify_reason: The comment at core/ConsumableMaster.lua:213-218 is false. It says the panel refresh keeps hydrating rows while the addon is off, but the stand-down calls UnregisterAllEvents (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:92), which removes GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED, and it drops the options bus target (settings/OptionsShim.lua:263+). Nothing reaches Recompute or PANEL_REFRESH while disabled. The recompute on re-enable comes from standUp's RequestRecompute (LifecycleSetup.lua:114-116), not from 'the toggle's onChange in settings/Panel.lua', so that pointer is stale. The rows fall back to [Loading] (modules/KCMItemRow.lua:88-99). The impact is cosmetic: only uncached, non-bag item names in a panel opened while disabled in a fresh session, and slash-commands.md:188 leaves the refresh subscription unruled. I lowered severity to low. The remediation (fix the comment, add a Known Limitations entry, owner decision on LoadItem) is right.

findings.title: Two hot-path item reads call the bare deprecated global GetItemInfo with no C_Item ladder; itemFields caches an unread subType
findings.evidence: The siblings core/Classifier.lua:165-169 and core/WeaponSlots.lua:46-49 already prefer C_Item with a guarded fallback. These two sites run on every recompute and every tooltip-cache fill. Whether 12.0.x still ships the global is unverified; if a patch removes it, ranking and tooltip parsing both fail. subType is fetched and cached but none of the 15 callers reads it.
findings.remediation: Add KCM.Compat.GetItemInfo in core/Compat.lua (C_Item.GetItemInfo first, the global as a guarded fallback) and route Ranker.itemFields and TooltipCache.Get through it. Drop subType from the fetch, the cache and the return, and update the 14 call sites (Ranker.lua:235-322 and :582) to destructure (quality, ilvl, tt). Add C_Item.GetItemInfo to tests/wow_mock.lua if it is missing, add a compat test, and compare the offline recompute B/iter against the 2551.1 baseline.
findings.verify_reason: Verified. modules/Ranker.lua:88 and core/TooltipCache.lua:459 call the bare GetItemInfo, which was deprecated in 11.0 in favour of C_Item.GetItemInfo. Anti-pattern #10 says to route deprecated APIs through Compat, and core/Compat.lua has no GetItemInfo wrapper. subType is fetched and cached (:88-95), but every caller discards it (the _ in the third slot at :235-322 and :582). There are 14 callers, not 15: the grep count of 15 includes the definition. I lowered severity to low because the global works on the current client and the breakage is hypothetical. This is a standards deviation with no reachable failure today. The remediation is correct. Note that the guarded fallbacks to the bare global in Classifier and KCMItemRow are acceptable ladders.

findings.title: 27 of the 33 LibKa0s tags vendored since 2026-08-25 have no docs/revendor/ bundle and no Documented deviations row
findings.evidence: The only bundle after v1.34.0 is 2026-09-23-v1.55.0 (v1.54.2 -> v1.55.0). The span v1.35.0 -> v1.53.0 (18 tags) and 9 earlier tags (v1.18.0-v1.29.0, excluding v1.25.0) went unrecorded. Graded High because AUDIT.md's re-vendor check says so explicitly. The impact is record-keeping only; step 5's impact table would make it Low.
findings.remediation: Write one consolidated bundle, docs/revendor/<date>-v1.53.0/ (01_DELTA.md and 05_SUMMARY.md), whose 01_DELTA.md names the span of 27 tags from v1.18.0 to v1.53.0 and the sweeps that vendored them, and whose 05_SUMMARY.md records the adoptions made along the way. Add a '## Documented deviations' row keyed audit-review-history that points at that bundle for the individual tags; E8 reads one tag per bundle, so the row is what clears the span. The S1-1 whole-folder re-vendor carries its own <date>-v<tag> bundle. Re-run E8 and confirm it comes out at 0.
findings.verify_reason: The evidence is accurate. docs/revendor has bundles only for v1.15.0, v1.25.0, v1.30.0, v1.31.0-v1.34.0 and v1.55.0, and running E8 (03_EVIDENCE.md:300-335) gives 27 unrecorded tags with no Documented deviations row. The audit-review-history MUST (line 34) and AUDIT.md's High grading (AUDIT.md:341) are cited correctly. However, the impact is record-keeping only, with no runtime or user effect, so I rated it low on reachable impact rather than on how strongly the rule is worded. The remediation needs one fix. E8 reads exactly one tag per bundle: the first vN.N.N in the folder name, or else the tail of 01_DELTA.md line 1. A consolidated folder named <date>-v1.18.0..v1.53.0 therefore records only v1.18.0 and leaves 26 tags flagged. The '## Documented deviations' row (the rule's own alternative, keyed audit-review-history) is required, not optional, for the span to clear E8.

findings.title: AUDIT.md grades the re-vendor check High, contradicting its own step-5 impact table; the check also cannot read a consolidated span bundle
findings.locations: WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md (re-vendor check; step 5 impact table)
findings.evidence: The re-vendor check says a tag vendored with no bundle and no row 'is a High finding'. Step 5 reserves High for user- or session-reachable defects, so a record-keeping gap becomes this addon's only High. E8 may also not recognise a consolidated span bundle as covering the tags in it.
findings.remediation: Upstream in WowAddonStandards: either grade the re-vendor check through step 5 (Low, still a MUST) or state explicitly that it is an exception. Make the check able to read a consolidated span bundle (01_DELTA.md naming the span).
findings.verify_reason: WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md:341-342 says a tag vendored with no bundle and no deviation row 'is a **High** finding'. The step-5 grading table at AUDIT.md:865 reserves High for defects a user, their SavedVariables or their session can hit today, and AUDIT.md:201 grades config and hygiene gaps as Low or Info. The two passages contradict each other, and the fix belongs upstream. The consolidated-bundle half is also fair: :343-347 recommend one consolidated bundle that names its span, but the check's trigger text (:322-341) only says 'a bundle naming it', so it does not say whether a bundle naming a span counts for each tag inside it.

findings.title: The host hand-rolls the settings open, category-ID capture and SetExpanded walk beside LibKa0s-Options-1.0's CreateOptionsPanel and OpenOptionsPanel
findings.evidence: O.Open calls Settings.OpenToCategory(KCM._settingsCategoryID) and privately copies the expand walk. The library's CreateOptionsPanel and OpenOptionsPanel are never called. The host copy is the only one that parks registration in combat, so it cannot be deleted until the library parks. The library's registerMain has no InCombatLockdown check.
findings.remediation: Upstream first (A3 / S0-3, LibKa0s-Options-1.0): CreateOptionsPanel refuses and parks under InCombatLockdown. Add O.ReplayPending(). OpenOptionsPanel returns a boolean. Add library tests for park, replay and idempotence. Tag, then re-vendor whole. Then B3 / S3-2: KCM.Options.Open delegates to UI.OpenOptionsPanel. registerPanel delegates to UI.CreateOptionsPanel, with buildMain and RegisterOptionsPage. Delete expandMainCategory and KCM._settingsCategoryID. Use the library's COMBAT_REFUSED wording. Add CreateOptionsPanel, OpenOptionsPanel and ReplayPending as stub no-ops, pinned by test_surface_parity. Rewrite the two registration cases against ReplayPending. If upstream declines, add a Documented deviations row keyed options-ui-§2 with the trigger 'the options library parks registration in combat'.
findings.verify_reason: settings/OptionsShim.lua:192-205 has a private expandMainCategory, and :207-236 has O.Open calling Settings.OpenToCategory(KCM._settingsCategoryID). settings/Panel.lua:1266-1286 parks registration under InCombatLockdown (registerPending) and sets KCM._settingsCategoryID. settings/OptionsSetup.lua:287-288 says outright that the addon never calls the library's CreateOptionsPanel. A grep found no host call to CreateOptionsPanel or OpenOptionsPanel. In libs/LibKa0s/Options.lua, registerMain (:1322-1344) has no combat check, and the only InCombatLockdown checks are :460 and OpenOptionsPanel :1412. So the library cannot replace the host's combat parking yet, and the upstream-first order in the remediation is right. Low is fair because the host copy works; this is duplication, not a user-facing defect.

findings.title: The kit's prose gate skips docs/automated-tests/ and docs/perf-analysis/ whole, hiding authored store-root files (README.md, RESULTS.md)

findings.title: The event registration block in KCM:OnEnable has no per-event pcall and no rejected-name record
findings.evidence: Nine bare self:RegisterEvent calls. All nine names are live today, so this is latent. A retired name would silently leave the addon deaf to every event registered after it, and standUp calls OnEnable too.
findings.remediation: B4 / S3-1 (after B1 and B2): a module-level EVENTS list and a safeRegister helper using pcall, front-gated by C_EventUtils.IsEventValid. Publish KCM.RejectedEvents and surface it in the [Init] debug content and a /cm dump events target. Add a mock.__badEvents case, with a falsification comment, where one retired name leaves the other eight bound. Point test_disabled step 1 at KCM.EVENTS. Note the trade in docs/midnight-quirks.md. Optional A4 / S0-4: a shared SafeRegister on LibKa0s-Core-1.0, then re-vendor; this is the owner's scheduling call, not a blocker.
findings.verify_reason: core/ConsumableMaster.lua:709-717 has nine bare self:RegisterEvent calls with no pcall and no record of rejected names. events-frames-taint §1 (lines 26-28 of that subsection) makes a pcall-isolated registration helper a MUST, makes a player-reachable record of rejected names a MUST, and makes IsEventValid a SHOULD front-gate. All nine names are valid on the live client, so the risk is latent and Low is right. The remediation matches the rule.

findings.title: Standing back up skips login's auto-discovery pass and stale-discovered sweep
findings.evidence: runAutoDiscovery and Selector.SweepStaleDiscovered run only in OnPlayerEnteringWorld, which does not fire again on re-enable. Non-seeded consumables looted while disabled are not candidates until the next BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED.
findings.remediation: C-05: extract P.DiscoverAndSweep(reason), call it from OnPlayerEnteringWorld and from standUp before RequestRecompute, and publish it as KCM.Pipeline.DiscoverAndSweep. Add the case 'Disabled 9c: an item looted while disabled is discovered on the way back up'.
findings.verify_reason: standUp (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:110-119) calls Bus.StandUp, KCM:OnEnable, MacroBar.Update and RequestRecompute('stand_up'), but no discovery. runAutoDiscovery and Selector.SweepStaleDiscovered run only in OnPlayerEnteringWorld (core/ConsumableMaster.lua:587-590) and OnBagUpdateDelayed (:609). standDown unregisters every event (:88), so bags looted while disabled go undiscovered until the next BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED. The impact is transient and self-heals, so low is right. KCM.Pipeline.RunAutoDiscovery already exists (:359), so the new P.DiscoverAndSweep can wrap it.

findings.title: The /cm resetall help text understates a whole-profile reset, and its two doors (popups, combat guard, refresh) diverge

KCM.ResetAllToDefaults refuses in combat (returns false, 'combat'). doResetAll drops its own guard. The OnAccept handler distinguishes combat from DB not ready. Optionally collapse to one popup. Add a combat-refusal case for both doors.

That is the targeted reset's wording (doResetAllPriorities), not the whole-profile act. The KCM_CONFIRM_RESET popup (core/SlashCommands.lua:41-61) and the KCM_RESET_ALL popup (settings/General.lua:146-159) duplicate each other. Only doResetAll (General.lua:107-118) combat-guards and calls H.RefreshAllPanels, while the comment at ConsumableMaster.lua:559 claims 'two doors cannot diverge'. options-ui.md §12 requires them to be the same act. The DB reset is combat-safe (per the General.lua comment), so the impact is UX and consistency only: low.

findings.title: Bare /cm bar toggle reads the latch-inclusive IsEnabled, so it never toggles off during a perf hold
findings.evidence: During a perf capture's suspended arm, it writes enabled = true and prints ON every time while the bar stays hidden.

findings.verify_reason: core/SlashCommands.lua:904 computes on = not KCM.MacroBarModel.IsEnabled(). core/MacroBarModel.lua:146-150 IsEnabled returns false whenever KCM.IsStoodDown() is true (the latch includes the perf suspended arm). So during a perf hold, bare /cm bar always computes on=true, writes enabled=true and prints ON. Real, low severity.

findings.title: The About page logo path hard-codes the ConsumableMaster folder name
findings.evidence: Every other media path derives from addonName (core/LauncherSetup.lua:107-108). A renamed install folder draws no logo.
findings.remediation: C-15: in settings/Panel.lua:148 build the path from the namespace: local LOGO_TEXTURE = ('Interface\\AddOns\\%s\\media\\logos\\%s.logo.tga'):format(KCM.name, KCM.name:lower()). Alternatively capture the first vararg (`local addonName, NS = ...`) and use that. Cite it as consistency with core/LauncherSetup.lua:107-108, not as a layout-§4 deviation.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Panel.lua:148 does hard-code [[Interface\AddOns\ConsumableMaster\media\logos\consumablemaster.logo.tga]], and core/LauncherSetup.lua:107-108 builds its path from addonName, so the inconsistency is real. The file exists under that name in media/logos/. Two corrections. (1) Rule ref: layout-§4 (standards/layout.md:116-127) only requires the file to be named <folder name, lowercased>.logo.tga so the path can be worked out. It does not require building the path at runtime, and the current literal meets it. So this is a consistency/robustness issue that only shows up on a renamed install folder, not a layout-§4 deviation. (2) Remediation: Panel.lua opens with `local _, NS = ...` (line 26), so there is no addonName local. It should use KCM.name (NS.name = addonName at core/Namespace.lua:13), not an undefined addonName.
